/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/items.source_en: Built around your all-aboard time, not a fixed clock

Standard group tours run on the operator's schedule, not yours. A private cruise excursion starts the moment you disembark and ends well before your all-aboard, with a 60-minute safety buffer that absorbs Seoul traffic. The driver-guide treats the ship's departure time as the only deadline that matters.
Pickup at the gangway, not 'meet at a station in Seoul'

Cruise terminals at Incheon are 50 km from central Seoul. Public transit means a taxi to Incheon Airport, then the AREX train, then a subway line, then walking — easily 90+ minutes each way and a real risk if delayed. A private car is direct, door-to-door, and your luggage stays in the vehicle if you want.
No mystery shopping stops, no group of 40

Many large cruise-line excursions include forced ginseng-shop or duty-free stops that eat 60–90 minutes of your day. A private car has no such commercial pressure: you stop where you want, for as long as you want, in your own group only.

Royal guard ceremony cancelled by rain? Skip Bukchon, add Jogyesa? Want to swap ⟦G0⟧ for the Korean War Memorial because your father served? All possible — a private guide-driver can rebuild the day mid-itinerary as long as the sailaway window holds.

/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/title.source_en: Why this route is built this way
/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/title.tm: Pourquoi cet itinéraire est conçu ainsi

/routeShapeIntro/subtitle.source_en: A point-to-point loop that starts and ends at your ship's gangway. The Seoul itinerary itself is a cluster, not a line — Gyeongbokgung, Bukchon, ⟦G1⟧, and ⟦G0⟧ are all within a 20-minute radius of each other, which is what makes a 7–9 hour port day workable. The driver-guide's main job, after the cultural commentary, is keeping your sail-away time visible at every transition.

/staticQuestions/0/answer.source_en: The driver-guide tracks the cruise schedule and adjusts pickup time accordingly. If the delay is significant (over 2 hours), the day's itinerary may need to be shortened — your guide will recommend the best subset to fit the remaining window.

/staticQuestions/0/question.source_en: What if my ship is delayed arriving at Incheon?

/staticQuestions/1/answer.source_en: Gyeongbokgung is closed on Tuesdays. If your port day falls on Tuesday, the substitute is Changdeokgung Palace and its UNESCO-listed Secret Garden (Huwon) — equally worth the visit, sometimes preferred by repeat visitors.

/staticQuestions/2/answer.source_en: Generally no — DMZ tours from Incheon are tight on time (DMZ is ≈ 50 km north of Seoul, the cruise terminal is ≈ 50 km west). For most cruise schedules, a DMZ + Seoul highlights combo doesn't fit. If your port call is 10+ hours and you want DMZ-only, ask in advance — a separate Incheon-DMZ private tour is offered.

/staticQuestions/2/question.source_en: Can we go to the DMZ instead?

/staticQuestions/3/answer.source_en: You provide the ship name, port-call date, expected arrival time, and all-aboard time at booking. The guide cross-checks against the published cruise itinerary and the Incheon Port Authority's daily schedule. Any change communicated by your cruise line should also be relayed to the guide via WhatsApp.

/staticQuestions/3/question.source_en: How does the guide know our ship's schedule?

/staticQuestions/4/answer.source_en: The tour runs in light rain. In a typhoon or heavy snow, the itinerary shifts indoors (palace covered halls, Jogyesa, ⟦G0⟧'s underground arcade, museum stops). The driver carries umbrellas. Outright cancellation only if a typhoon also cancels your ship's port call.

/staticQuestions/4/question.source_en: What if there's heavy rain or a typhoon?

/staticQuestions/5/answer.source_en: Yes — many cruise guests use the day to also handle a hotel transfer or duty-free errand with luggage on board. The vehicle is locked when not in use; valuables should still be carried with you. Luggage capacity depends on vehicle size, so advise volume in advance.

/staticQuestions/5/question.source_en: Can we leave luggage in the car?

/staticQuestions/6/answer.source_en: Yes — it covers the most distinctive stops in the area in a single balanced day.
/staticQuestions/6/answer.tm: Oui — il couvre les arrêts les plus caractéristiques de la région en une seule journée équilibrée.

/staticQuestions/6/question.source_en: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to Seoul?

/staticQuestions/7/answer.source_en: Moderate walking with some active sections.
/staticQuestions/7/answer.tm: Marche modérée avec quelques sections plus actives.

/staticQuestions/8/answer.source_en: Yes for families whose kids can handle a full day of moving around.

/staticQuestions/8/question.source_en: Is this tour suitable for families?

/staticQuestions/9/answer.source_en: Yes for active seniors; less ideal for low-mobility travelers.

/staticQuestions/9/question.tm: Les personnes âgées peuvent-elles participer confortablement ?

/staticQuestions/10/answer.source_en: Best fit is around age 6 and up — children comfortable with a full-day rhythm and the walking notes above.

/seasonalVariations/0/description.source_en: Cherry blossoms at Gyeongbokgung and along the Cheonggyecheon Stream; Bukchon's traditional houses in spring greens.

/seasonalVariations/1/description.source_en: Long daylight hours mean you can squeeze N Seoul Tower into a tight window; many indoor museum options if it's hot.

/seasonalVariations/2/description.source_en: Maple foliage at Gyeongbokgung's rear garden (Hyangwonjeong) and along Bukchon ridges; clearest air for tower viewpoints.

/seasonalVariations/3/description.source_en: Snow on the palace courtyards is one of Seoul's classic photographs; fewer crowds at major sites.
